scope: Independent visual audit of Cod. Sang. 756 pages 8 and 9 only; no Voynich target or Turner classification data used.

source.manuscript_date: first half of the fifteenth century (institutional metadata)

orientation.ring_order: The lists below preserve physical quadrant order and, within each quadrant, clockwise order from the top-right sector. This is a page orientation convention, not a generation order.

p8.layout: Two horizontal diagram rows, with six visible figure cells in each row; surrounding prose and colored rubrics.
observations: The page visibly distinguishes fixed and mobile/contradictory diagram material by headings and ink color.
No complete sixteen-name ring or explicit four-element ownership legend was securely read on page 8.
Page 8 therefore does not by itself certify a complete early program.

p9.layout: A circular Thema diagram with two separately named concentric sixteen-entry bands, dot figures between/around them, a four-way cross, and cardinal labels.

upper_right.raw_visual: grey cursive fragment, partly crossed by radial lines

lower_right.raw_visual: grey cursive fragment, partly crossed by radial lines

lower_left.raw_visual: grey cursive fragment, partly crossed by radial lines

upper_left.raw_visual: grey cursive fragment, partly crossed by radial lines

p9.central_label_result: Four grey central-quarter inscriptions are visible, but their letter sequences and quadrant boundaries are not secure enough for a responsible transcription from these images. No element word is promoted from visual resemblance.

explicitly_shown: Two distinct named sixteen-entry figure bands.
Dot figures associated spatially with the rings.
not_explicitly_licensed_by_this_audit: An element class for any ring or sector.
Ownership of a central grey label by an outer or inner ring.
A mapping between the two named rings or a generation direction.
classification_assessment.element_ownership: Not established. Adjacency to a quadrant is not treated as ownership without a readable legend, arrow, or prose statement.

limits: The figure-name readings are direct visual readings with marked uncertainty, not a modern dictionary substitution.
Central quarter labels remain unresolved rather than being filled from a later source.
This is source evidence from an earlier fifteenth-century manuscript witness, not a Voynich reading or a confirmation of any target hypothesis.
